acceptance: A core dry run reports a missing or wrongly scoped delivery App installation.
A fork dry run reports Issues disabled and a missing controller App installation.
Neither check needs or exposes a write credential; tests cover present, missing and wrongly scoped cases.
description:
Problem. Both SQLGlot automation dry runs succeed without checking what their write paths need, so a misconfiguration surfaces only on the first real run. Core: the sqlglot-delivery.yml dry run 42298338422 passed, but the first enabled run 42326369414 failed at 'Mint the App token' with 404 on GET /repos/BenchBox-dev/BenchBox/installation because the delivery App was created but not installed on the repository. Fork: the controller files refresh conflicts and failures as issues, but BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot has Issues disabled (has_issues=false, read live 2026-11-07); every dry run passed and a real failure would fail the publish job and lose the report. Covers both repositories: the fork check lands through a fork PR.

Change. Add a prerequisite readback to each dry run that needs no write credential: core confirms the delivery App is installed on this repository with exactly contents and pull-requests write; fork confirms Issues are enabled and the controller App is installed on the fork only. Report missing prerequisites in the job summary, and fail the enabled path before any mutation.
